runtime.execution: Rust provider/turn core and daemon supervisor/workers; per-session owned CPython stdio kernel on one asyncio loop; bash background process groups, RLM child sessions and independent provider requests.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns session workers, Python namespaces, child/batch process containment and JSON harness stores; consumes providers/MCP; kernels are session-owned rather than shared fabric consumers.

summary: Code-first coding agent: the shipped model tool is ipython; Python composes host skills, shell handles, RLM child sessions and mutable harness state.

inspection.scope: Shipped tool selection/loop→kernel provision/execute/result→host bridge→family routing, compaction/refine settlement, snapshot limits/cleanup; scripted continuation and busy delivery test assertions.
inspection.limits: Source read only, reference not executed. No reference execution. Rust port retains misleading TypeScript comments in Python skills. Snapshot persistence omits unsafe/unpicklable/oversize namespace objects and does not preserve live process/socket identity. Refinement governs prompt/memory/skill/subagent entries, not executable rebuild and validated autoresearch.

actions.name: ipython
actions.lifecycle: Sequential cell in owned persistent Python namespace; abort can leave busy kernel needing wait/kill
actions.authority: Model code has ordinary filesystem/import/host authority, no tool approval gate traced here

actions.name: bash; BashHandle.pid/running/output/tail/poll/kill; await handle
actions.lifecycle: Starts immediately; foreground cancellation kills group; released background work survives cell abort but not kernel teardown
actions.authority: Model via Python; owned host process group

actions.name: rlm.spawn; rlm.create_session; rlm.find_models; rlm.list_subagents; rlm.collect; rlm.delete_subagent
actions.lifecycle: Independent child sessions retained until deletion; collect nonblocking or bounded await
actions.authority: Model Python host bridge; direct-family lifecycle; create_session daemon root only

actions.input: message, receiver_role parent/sibling/child and receiver_name; broadcast all
actions.lifecycle: Busy target queued with queuedAt; role/family route; peer then supervisor fallback
actions.authority: Model skill inside kernel; paused/capacity gates

actions.name: agent_observe.list_agents/get_agent/recent_messages
actions.output: Family/session state and bounded message previews

actions.name: HarnessState.get/list/search/create/update/delete; create_memory/create_prompt_note/create_skill/create_subagent; record_refinement

actions.lifecycle: Settings/auth/MCP next-use refresh; no executable recompile

filesystem.detail: Python ordinary file APIs and skill imports compose edits/search; not dedicated JSON tools in shipped surface.

processes.detail: Immediate shell handles, bounded tail/poll/group kill, foreground versus released-background cancellation semantics.

code_actions.detail: Python code cells compose bash/host skills/child calls and normal programs.

persistent_kernel.detail: Session-owned CPython namespace persists; snapshots selectively dill variables with16MiB/256MiB limits; handles/threads/sockets cannot be assumed restored.

standing_database.detail: Queryable mutable local/global structured HarnessState JSON entries and refinements; not a general shared SQL service.

workflow_programming.detail: Python code, named skills/subagent definitions and child APIs supply programmable composition; full turn scheduler remains Rust hooks.

multi_model.detail: Model lookup and per-child model/thinking selection; simultaneous independent child sessions rather than only UI switch.

live_collaboration.detail: Model role-addressed/broadcast messages with receipts and busy-target queue; bounded ingestion and pause gate, no blind retry.

concurrent_work.detail: RLM child sessions and released background bash handles can outlive one cell; Python execution cells remain sequential.

steering_interrupt.detail: Loop steering/follow-up polling and abort; Python interrupt recovery distinguishes busy previous cell; shell foreground versus background semantics.

turn_redefinition.detail: Rust API offers steering/continuation/stop hooks; model changes skills/subagent/prompt entries, not arbitrary Rust scheduling body in flight.

compaction.detail: Automatic/manual/model-scheduled summaries retain tail anchor/previous summary; durable notice explicitly prunes oversized kernel names.

context_repair.detail: Retained session entries and bounded family previews plus Python file access can compose retrieval; no exposed original-complete repair action traced.

original_audit.detail: Session/refinement/compaction durable records preserve important transitions, but diagnostic rotation/output bounds and namespace loss preclude complete original IO claim.

audit_query.detail: Python file reading and bounded family recent-message APIs support inspection; structured harness search queries memories, not complete original transport audit.

hot_change.detail: Model mutates harness entries; host refit rebuilds system prompt after settled turn; settings/auth/MCP resolved per use, executable unchanged.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Kernel/session snapshot restoration and daemon lifecycle are partial continuity primitives; no actual executable self-compile/quiescent outpost handoff traced.

remote_services.detail: Consumes providers and MCP through host/Python bridge; owns per-session kernels and child processes rather than shared kernel service consumer boundary.

self_improvement.detail: Dedicated plan/apply/rollback of harness entry definitions and automatic review gates exist; expected outcomes/history are not discriminating experiment/evaluation governance or executable rebuild.

complaints.detail: Not established in the inspected entry, model loop, action dispatch and state paths; no universal absence claim.

authority.detail: Shipped ipython allows model authored ordinary Python and host skill/harness mutations; scope/relationship constraints around global stores and family delivery.

evaluation.detail: Scripted model continuation oracle checks actual second-request ID/result ordering; busy message oracle checks queued receipt. Mocks do not validate live provider/kernel/platform behavior.

time_order.detail: Explicit scheduled heartbeat run times/state and awaited-handle lifecycle; monotonic timeout/cancellation boundary supports local ordering, not cross-system original causal ledger.

evidence.claim: Effective shipped tool selection is ipython, not independent shell/edit JSON tools.
Single sequential code-string tool forwards to persistent kernel with structured outputs/attachments/errors.
Continuation pairs tool results; steering/follow-up/continuation/stop hooks and abort checks govern boundaries.
Persistent namespace compiles/executes Python cell with async support and error/interrupt events.
BashHandle exposes pid/running/output/tail/poll/kill with process group escalation.
Foreground await cancellation kills command group; released background handle survives cell cancellation, owned until kernel teardown.
Namespace snapshot caps are 16MiB per variable and 256MiB aggregate with saved/skipped/pruned manifest.
Dill per-name snapshot skips failures/size excess, stages payload/manifest and may prune oversize live names.
Last shared inner owner drop performs best-effort hard cleanup.
Graceful snapshot/host drain/protocol shutdown followed by deadline cleanup and orphan-group reaping.
Model-accessible HarnessState uses structured local/global JSON with mtime reload.
Harness entries can be fetched/deleted/listed/created, persisted with explicit scope.
Refinement records evidence/outcome and small-edit planning, not an experiment oracle.
RLM spawn/create_session/model lookup uses host bridge and returns stable child/session handles.
RLM collect polls or bounded waits for retained direct-child results, no parent steering.
Family controller uses durable identity, peer transport then supervisor fallback; no blind retry of non-idempotent sends.
Role-addressed/broadcast send calls host bridge and returns delivery receipts.
Busy-worker test asserts queued status/time rather than silently dropping or denying delivery.
Pending compact/refine consumed at settled boundary, compact then refine; summarizer gets its own cancellation slot.
Compaction prunes oversized variables and appends namespace/persistence notice.
Summary request includes previous summary and authoritative retained-tail anchor.
Refinement durable audit type, auto review defaults/gates, local scope guard and model-facing outcome/notice.
Plan requests scoped JSON entry edits; apply handles rollback/result, not harness executable compilation.
Reload resolves settings/auth/MCP per use; command succeeds without executable reload.
Read-only family listing/live summaries/bounded recent message previews.
Tool continuation oracle inspects second request exact user/assistant/toolResult pairing and ID.
Standing heartbeat state includes schedule/next/last run/status/count and steer/follow-up delivery.
Kernel stderr tails/log budgets/rotation bound retained diagnostic bytes.

tests.oracle: Second scripted provider call must include matching tool-call ID/result and correct role order; scripted transport only.
Worker busy flag forces queued receipt/queuedAt and queue content assertions; no live-model delivery exercised.
Probe fixtures require prune notice/name list; a mocked namespace probe does not establish dill or OS serialization safety.

strengths: Code-first single tool gives model a compact compositional surface.
Harness entry changes and compact/refine are scheduled at a meaningful settled boundary.
Busy-target receipts and explicit foreground/background process ownership are unusually precise.
limits: No reference execution. Rust port retains misleading TypeScript comments in Python skills. Snapshot persistence omits unsafe/unpicklable/oversize namespace objects and does not preserve live process/socket identity. Refinement governs prompt/memory/skill/subagent entries, not executable rebuild and validated autoresearch.
arconaut_questions: Which standing services should become external consumers instead of owned per-session kernels?
Can refinement expected outcomes be replaced with explicit direct-property oracles and experiment lineage?
Which transcript/kernel snapshot omissions must trigger model-readable continuity warnings and repair paths?
